result:
Reader was right — redesigned in `scenario.json` rather than reworded.

What changed: the scenario no longer acts on the calendar itself or names metadata fields. The request is now "Set the location of the interview panel on the Field Hiring calendar about onsite interviews to Building 4, Room 402." — an event action identified the way a user would say it: event title, calendar name, and the calendar's topic ("about onsite interviews" = its description, attached to the nearest noun "calendar"). The time-zone condition is gone entirely.

Kept by judgment: the same-titled "Field Hiring" calendars remain, since they are the honest reason a user adds a topic disambiguator at all; a careful colleague reads "calendar about onsite interviews" as the calendar's own topic, which the location-mention (F1) and event-mention (F2) decoys do not satisfy. Decoy set is unchanged in kind — F1 location-substitute, F2 event-description indirection (now a separate "Logistics note" event so the witness panel itself is clean), F0 plain — with the reference query re-rooted at `calendar_events` joining its calendar, and background events (`Picnic planning`, `Offer review`) each failing at least two conditions.
